_comment: Real-world counterparts for worlds in the atlas. These are NOT illustrative art: each is an actual photograph of the real object, place or event that a fiction's chronology leans on, which is the honest visual companion to a chart whose whole claim is provenance. Every entry is fetched from Wikimedia Commons and its licence verified at fetch time; anything that is neither public domain nor a CC attribution licence is refused rather than guessed at.

2001-space-odyssey.caption: Earthrise, photographed from lunar orbit by Apollo 8, 24 December 1968
2001-space-odyssey.why: The real photograph of the real achievement the film extrapolates from four years later.

interstellar.caption: Saturn at equinox, imaged by the Cassini orbiter
interstellar.why: The film routes its wormhole past Saturn, using the real planet as the last familiar landmark.

the-expanse.caption: Mars in true colour, imaged by Rosetta's OSIRIS camera
the-expanse.why: The world the series spends two centuries terraforming, photographed as it actually is.

contact.caption: The Very Large Array radio telescope, New Mexico
contact.why: The real instrument and the real technique the novel's Search for Extra-Terrestrial Intelligence depends on.

dune.caption: Sand dunes of the Tadrart Acacus, Libya
dune.why: Standing in for Arrakis: the desert ecology Herbert actually researched.

fallout.caption: The Trinity test, 16 July 1945
fallout.why: The real detonation behind the fictional Great War of 2077 and its whole aesthetic.

children-of-men.caption: The London skyline
children-of-men.why: The city the film renders as a fortified, exhausted state in 2027.

warhammer-40000.caption: The Pillars of Creation, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
warhammer-40000.why: A real glimpse of the galactic scale the setting claims as its canvas.

star-trek.caption: The Blue Marble, photographed by Apollo 17, 7 December 1972
star-trek.why: The image that shaped the optimism the series is built on, taken five years after it first aired.
